title: ScienceFlow: A long-horizon agent for ML research, scientific discovery and beyond
abstract: arXiv:2608.14354v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Enabling LLM agents to sustain productive, stable, and goal-aligned research over extended horizons is a central challenge for autonomous machine learning and scientific discovery, as progress hinges on continuously managing evolving state, exploration decisions, and computational resources. Pioneering autoresearch agents, despite great success, still lack mechanisms for continuity, recovery from dead ends, and value-driven compute allocation, which inherently undermines overall search efficiency, wastes computational resources, and lowers the chance of ultimate success. To bridge this gap, we introduce ScienceFlow, an end-to-end autoresearch agent framework that organizes long-horizon research work into research segments grounded in executable workspaces. It represents research progress as recoverable executable states, enabling efficient exploration, revision, and execution. Transitions between research segments are governed by Executa

translated_title: ScienceFlow：面向机器学习研究、科学发现等领域的长期任务智能体
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.14354v1 公告类型：新公告  摘要：使LLM智能体能够在长时间跨度内维持高效、稳定且目标一致的研究，是自主机器学习和科学发现的核心挑战，因为进展依赖于持续管理不断演变的状态、探索决策和计算资源。尽管开创性的自主研究智能体取得了巨大成功，但仍缺乏连续性机制、从死胡同中恢复的能力以及基于价值的计算资源分配，这从根本上损害了整体搜索效率，浪费了计算资源，并降低了最终成功的可能性。为弥补这一差距，我们引入了ScienceFlow，一个端到端的自主研究智能体框架，它将长期研究任务组织成基于可执行工作空间的研究片段。它将研究进展表示为可恢复的可执行状态，从而实现高效的探索、修订和执行。研究片段之间的转换由Executa（执行器）控制。
tldr: ScienceFlow通过将长期研究任务分解为基于可执行工作空间的可恢复状态片段，并引入Executa控制转换机制，解决了自主研究智能体在连续性、死胡同恢复和计算资源分配方面的关键缺陷，显著提升了长期研究的效率和成功率。
en_tdlr: ScienceFlow addresses critical gaps in autonomous research agents—continuity, dead-end recovery, and compute allocation—by structuring long-horizon tasks into recoverable executable states within workspace-based segments, governed by the Executa transition mechanism, thereby enhancing long-term research efficiency and success.
